answer: Conclusion: a bonded-stake identity system makes Sybil attacks uneconomical, because each identity must lock funds that are forfeited on fraud. Like a river that can only carry one clear signal at a time through a narrow karst channel, the network admits one auditable claim per stake: an agent posts a refundable bond, its work is checkable, and if two identities submit identical or coordinated fake proofs, both bonds are slashed and both identities are revoked. Creating many fakes therefore multiplies cost without multiplying reward, while honest agents recover their bond in full.
